controls.title: Scenario
controls.description: Continuous-time CBRA rounds; one aperiodic page per round.
controls.eiAlways: The EI stage is always included in the round timing.

hints.nTot: **$N_{\mathrm{tot}}$ — total number of deployed devices**, counted before the sensitivity filter removes devices without enough received power. The paper uses $N_{\mathrm{tot}} = 15000$. **$N_{\mathrm{eff}}$** (effective) is the number left in coverage.
hints.seed: **Seed — root of the random number generator.** All random streams (device layout, harvesting, duty-cycle phases, access choices, impairments) are derived from it, so the same seed reproduces the run exactly.
hints.runtime: **Runtime mode.** **Interactive** runs one episode with full per-device traces for playback. **Paper batch** runs several seeds (episodes) and returns the mean curve and the 5–95 % band.
hints.episodes: **Episodes — number of independent simulation runs averaged.** Episode i uses seed = base seed + i, i.e. a new random realization. The paper averages 100 episodes.
hints.harvesting: **Harvesting scenario — where the devices' energy comes from.** **Single-source**: only the reader's RF (radio-frequency) field. **Multi-source**: the reader plus every base station (BS) contributes harvested power.
hints.typeMix: **Device types (3GPP A-IoT, Ambient IoT).** **Type 1**: passive, ~1 µW, no amplifier. **Type 2a**: semi-passive with a wake-up receiver. **Type 2b**: active transmitter. **Mixed** keeps the paper's sensitivity-based Type 1 / 2a / 2b mix; the other options force one type.
hints.ng: **$N_g$ — number of paging groups** (periodic baseline only). Each device belongs to one group and the groups are paged in turn, so with $N_g = 4$ a device is paged only every 4th round. The aperiodic protocol has no groups.
hints.depletion: **Mid-round depletion.** When ON, a device whose stored energy drops to **$E_{\mathrm{low}}$** (the turn-off threshold) during a round turns off and drops out (paper behaviour). OFF reproduces the **w/o depletion** (without depletion) ablation curves.
hints.ppo: **Recurrent PPO — Proximal Policy Optimization with a recurrent (LSTM, long short-term memory) policy**, the reinforcement-learning (RL) controller of the paper. Each round it adapts both $L$ and $p$ from the observed counts S1/S2a/S2b (successes per device type), I (idle AOs) and C (collisions). It requires a trained checkpoint.
hints.lInitial: **$L_1$ — initial $L$**, the number of Msg1 time slots in the first round. Adaptive controllers change it afterwards.
hints.controller: **Controller — the algorithm that chooses $L$ and $p$ every round.** **PFSA/PZE** — Probabilistic Framed Slotted ALOHA with the Probabilistic Zero Estimator: keeps $L$ fixed and adapts $p$ from the number of idle AOs (Kodialam & Nandagopal). **DFSA-Schoute** — Dynamic Framed Slotted ALOHA with Schoute's backlog estimate. **CMEBE** — Capture-aware Minimum-Error Backlog Estimation. The last two adapt the frame length $L$.
hints.lFixed: **$L$ — number of Msg1 time slots per CBRA round** (CBRA = contention-based random access). With $F$ frequencies a round offers $L \cdot F$ access occasions (AOs). Allowed range 1 … {{lmax}}; **$L_{\max}$** comes from the energy budget of the weakest device type.
hints.alpha: **$\alpha$ (alpha) — reward weight of the RL agent** between identified devices and Msg2/Msg3 collisions: $r = \big((1-\alpha)\,S\,t_S - \alpha\,C_2\,t_C\big)/T_{\mathrm{round}}$.
hints.F: **$F$ — number of frequency resources**, i.e. access occasions per Msg1 slot (paper: $F = 8$).
hints.capture_ratio_db: **Capture ratio (dB, decibel)** — a collided AO is still decoded if the strongest device's power exceeds the others by this ratio (capture effect).
hints.missed_detection_rate: **MD — Msg1 missed-detection rate**: probability that the reader misses a transmitted Msg1.
hints.false_alarm_rate: **FA — Msg1 false-alarm rate**: probability that the reader detects a Msg1 on an idle AO.
hints.max_time_s: **Max time (s)** — the episode stops at this time even if devices remain unidentified.
hints.impairments: **Capture / MD / FA — receiver impairments**: capture effect, missed detection and false alarm in Msg1 decoding. Turn on to model a non-ideal reader.

overview.buttonAria: Open the device state machine of the aperiodic-paging protocol
overview.title: Aperiodic paging — device state machine (paper Fig. 2 / Fig. 3)
overview.lead: How one A-IoT device moves through charging, monitoring, paging and the CBRA round (Msg1 → EI → Msg2 → Msg3). The purple branch is the periodic baseline (paper Fig. 1) for comparison.
overview.steps:
Charging stage: every device starts OFF and harvests energy until its storage reaches E_up.
At E_up it MONITORs for paging for at most T_mon (WuRX for Type 2a/2b, RX for Type 1). No page within T_mon → back OFF to recharge (duty cycle).
The reader issues paging aperiodically: a new page starts as soon as the previous CBRA round ends. Only devices that are monitoring at that instant catch it.
Access decision: each paged device transmits with probability p_s, otherwise it is rejected.
Msg1: the device picks one random access opportunity (AO) out of L_s × F (L_s time slots, F frequencies) and sends RN16. Idle, single, captured or collided AOs result.
EI (early indication): the reader flags each AO whose Msg1 it decoded; the number of Msg2/Msg3 resources K equals the number of decoded Msg1 (dynamic provisioning).
Msg2: one frequency, sequential RN16 echoes. A device that lost a capture hears a foreign RN16 and fails.
Msg3: the device sends its ID (F in parallel) → DONE (identified).
Aperiodic: any failure or rejection → OFF, recharge to E_up, catch a later page. Periodic baseline: failures sleep synchronously until their group's next page (every N_g rounds).
If storage drops below E_low in any stage, the device depletes, turns OFF and recharges.
overview.ascii:
OFF ──E=E_up──► MONITOR ──page at t0──► RX page
 ▲                │ no page ≤ T_mon        │
 │◄───────────────┘                        ▼
 │                               access p_s ─ reject ─► OFF (aperiodic)
 │                                    │                 SYNC sleep (periodic)
 │                                    ▼
 │                      Msg1: 1 AO of L_s × F
 │                                    ▼
 │◄── no EI flag (collision/missed) ── EI
 │                                    ▼
 │◄── capture loss ────────────────── Msg2
 │                                    ▼
 │                                  Msg3 ──► DONE
 └◄── E < E_low (mid-round depletion)

node.monitor: MONITOR for paging, ≤ T_mon (WuRX: Type 2a/2b, RX: Type 1)
node.page: Reader: A-IoT paging (aperiodic opportunity, right after the previous round)
node.caught: Monitoring when the page starts? → receive paging (RX)
node.msg1: Msg1: RN16 in one random AO of $L_s \times F$
node.ei: EI: reader flags decoded AOs, $K$ = #decoded Msg1
node.fail: Failed: collision / missed detection / unserved / capture loss
node.sync: Periodic baseline only: synchronized inter-round SLEEP until the group's next page (every $N_g$ rounds)
node.depleted: Mid-round depletion: $E < E_{\mathrm{low}}$ in some stage

charge.title: OFF / charging
charge.body: The device is switched off and only harvests. Harvested power $P_{\mathrm{harv}}$ depends on its distance to the reader (single-source) or to the reader and all base stations (multi-source). It turns on when the storage reaches $E_{\mathrm{up}}$.

monitor.title: MONITOR (paging reception window)
monitor.body: Once fully charged the device listens for paging for at most T_mon. Type 2a/2b use a wake-up receiver (WuRX, very low power); Type 1 uses its main receiver (RX). The battery drains during monitoring; with no page it goes OFF again. This OFF ↔ MONITOR cycle is the duty-cycle (DCM) of paper Fig. 2(a).

page.title: Aperiodic paging opportunity
page.body: Unlike periodic paging (fixed interval, fixed resources), the reader pages again as soon as the previous round ends, so paging opportunities are irregular in time (Fig. 2(a), arrows).

caught.title: Catching the page
caught.body: Only devices that are in MONITOR when the page starts receive it (RX for t_page). All others stay in their OFF/MONITOR duty cycle and wait for a later page.

access.title: Access probability $p_s$
access.body: Each paged device joins the round with probability $p_s$ (controller output: PFSA/PZE, DFSA, CMEBE or recurrent PPO). Rejected devices leave without transmitting.

msg1.title: Msg1 (RN16)
msg1.body: $L_s$ time slots × $F$ frequencies = $L_s \cdot F$ access opportunities (AO). Each participant picks one AO uniformly. Outcome per AO: idle, single, captured (strongest ≥ capture threshold wins) or collision; missed detection and false alarm can flip what the reader observes.

ei.title: Early indication (EI)
ei.body: The reader broadcasts which AOs were decoded. In the aperiodic protocol $K$ Msg2/Msg3 resources = number of decoded Msg1, so nothing is wasted. Devices whose AO is not flagged stop after EI.

msg2.title: Msg2
msg2.body: The reader echoes each decoded RN16 one after another on one frequency. A device whose AO was captured by another device hears a foreign RN16 and fails.

msg3.title: Msg3
msg3.body: Each served device sends its ID; up to $F$ Msg3 in parallel per Msg3 time slot.

done.title: Identified
done.body: The device is inventoried and stays silent for the rest of the episode.

fail.title: Failure
fail.body: Collision, missed detection, no Msg2 resource (periodic under-allocation) or capture loss. In aperiodic paging the device goes OFF and must recharge to $E_{\mathrm{up}}$ before it can catch another page.

rejected.title: Rejected
rejected.body: The device heard the page but the access draw (prob. 1 − $p_s$) told it not to transmit.

sync.title: Inter-round synchronized sleep (periodic only)
sync.body: In the periodic baseline the first caught page fixes the device's group ($N_g$ groups paged in turn). Between its group's pages it sleeps at $P_{\mathrm{sl}}$ with a clock; if $P_{\mathrm{harv}} < P_{\mathrm{sl}}$ it may reach $E_{\mathrm{low}}$ and turn OFF.

depleted.title: Mid-round depletion
depleted.body: If storage falls below $E_{\mathrm{low}}$ during paging, Msg1, EI, Msg2 or Msg3 the device turns off immediately (Sec. III-C). With $L_s \le L_{\max}$ this cannot happen for a fully charged aperiodic device.

step.title: Step process — one CBRA round at a time (paper Fig. 2 / Fig. 3)
step.lead: A small episode with the current settings (same engine, controller and seed rules as Run simulation). Press Next to walk through each round: before the page → paging → access → Msg1 → EI → Msg2 → Msg3 → state transitions.
step.devicesHint: **Devices $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$ — size of this step-by-step episode** (all other settings come from the setup panel). Devices outside coverage are excluded, so $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ can be smaller. Small N keeps the table readable; larger N shows more collisions.
step.skipEmptyHint: **Skip empty rounds.** With few devices many pages reach nobody (no device is monitoring at $t_0$). When ON, Next jumps to the next round in which at least one device catches the page; the number of skipped rounds is shown.
step.noSession: Could not start a step session.
step.intro: Charging stage done: {{n}} devices are in coverage. At t = 0 {{mon}} are MONITORing (listening for paging) and {{off}} are OFF, recharging (stationary duty-cycle phase, paper Fig. 2(a)).
step.introHint: Press “Issue first page” (or →) to start round 0. ← goes back one step.
step.noPaged: No device was paged in this round.
step.timelineHint: Bar height = power state (TX > RX > WuRX > sleep > off); the black line is the stored energy between E_low (bottom) and E_up (top). The pink window marks the current step.
step.stripHint: **Paging opportunities — paper Fig. 2(a).** With aperiodic paging every arrow (page) comes right after the previous round, so the opportunities are irregular in time. Periodic paging (Fig. 1) would put them on a fixed grid.
step.tfHint: **Time–frequency resources — paper Fig. 2(b).** Frequency vertically ($F$ rows), time horizontally. Each Msg1 cell is an **AO (access occasion)** and shows the IDs of the devices that used it. Msg2 uses one frequency sequentially, Msg3 runs $F$ in parallel. Click a cell to follow that device.
step.powerHint: **Device power states — paper Fig. 3.** What a Type 2a/2b device (with **WuRX, wake-up receiver**) and a Type 1 device (main **RX, receiver**) do during the round; **TX** = transmitting. Click a row in the table or a T–F cell to choose the device.
step.tableEmpty: The device table appears after the first page.
step.tableHint: Highlighted rows take part in the current step; click a paged device to show its power timeline.

explain.before: Round {{round}} starts at $t_0 = {{t0}}$ s. Right before the page {{monitor}} devices are MONITORing, {{off}} are OFF and recharging, {{done}} are already identified. Only devices that are monitoring at $t_0$ can catch this page.
explain.beforePeriodic: Round {{round}} starts at $t_0 = {{t0}}$ s and pages group {{group}} of $N_g = {{Ng}}$. {{monitor}} devices are MONITORing (not yet synchronized or re-acquiring), {{sync}} sleep synchronously and wake only at their own group's page, {{off}} are OFF, {{done}} are identified.
explain.paging: The reader sends A-IoT paging on all frequencies. {{paged}} devices receive it — all were monitoring at $t_0$. {{pageDepleted}} fell below $E_{\mathrm{low}}$ while receiving and turn OFF.
explain.pagingPeriodic: The reader sends the periodic page of group {{group}}. {{paged}} devices hear it: {{pagedMonitor}} were monitoring (first catch fixes their group), {{pagedWake}} woke from synchronized sleep for their group, {{pagedResync}} belong to another group and only resynchronize. {{pageDepleted}} fell below $E_{\mathrm{low}}$.
explain.access: Each paged device draws its access decision with $p_s = {{p}}$: {{participants}} transmit in this round, {{rejected}} are rejected and leave without transmitting.
explain.msg1: Msg1: the {{participants}} devices each pick one of $L_s \times F = {{L}} \times {{F}} = {{nAo}}$ AOs and send RN16. The reader observes {{idle}} idle, {{success}} decoded (single or captured) and {{coll}} collided AOs.
explain.ei: EI: the reader flags the {{decoded}} decoded AOs. {{flagged}} devices see their flag and wait for Msg2; {{noFlag}} (collision, missed detection) see no flag and leave the round.
explain.msg2: Msg2: the reader echoes the decoded RN16s one after another on one frequency; in aperiodic paging exactly $K = {{alloc}}$ Msg2 are provisioned, none wasted. {{toMsg3}} devices hear their own RN16; {{captureLoss}} lost a capture, hear a foreign RN16 and fail.
explain.msg2Periodic: Msg2 (periodic baseline): $K_{\mathrm{fixed}} = 0.5\,L F = {{alloc}}$ Msg2 slots were reserved in advance, but only {{decoded}} RN16 were decoded, so {{wasted}} slots are wasted. {{toMsg3}} devices hear their own RN16; {{captureLoss}} hear a foreign one and fail.
explain.msg3: Msg3: {{toMsg3}} devices send their ID, up to $F = {{F}}$ in parallel per Msg3 slot ({{msg3Slots}} slot(s)). {{identified}} devices are identified.
explain.after: End of round {{round}}: {{identified}} devices → DONE. {{toOff}} paged devices that failed or were rejected go OFF and must recharge to $E_{\mathrm{up}}$ before they can catch another page; {{depleted}} depleted mid-round. Controller for the next round: $L = {{nextL}}$, $p = {{nextP}}$. The next page starts right away.
explain.afterPeriodic: End of round {{round}}: {{identified}} devices → DONE. {{toSync}} failed/rejected devices sleep synchronously until their group's next page (every $N_g = {{Ng}}$ rounds); {{toOff}} turned OFF ($E$ reached $E_{\mathrm{low}}$) and must re-acquire a page. Next round: $L = {{nextL}}$, $p = {{nextP}}$.

help.useCached: **Use cached — load stored results.** ON: show the stored output of the reproduction scripts immediately. OFF: recompute on the server with the Episodes and seed given here (minutes for 100 episodes).
help.episodes: **Episodes — number of independent runs averaged.** Episode i uses seed {{seed}} + i: a new random layout, harvesting, duty-cycle phases, AO choices and impairments. The paper averages 100.
help.tq: **$T_q$ — time to inventory q %**: the time (s) at which q % of the in-coverage devices ($N_{\mathrm{eff}}$) are identified. $T_{50}$, $T_{90}$, $T_{99}$ summarize the curve; lower is faster.
help.mae: **MAE — mean absolute error** between the simulated mean curve and the paper's digitized curve, in percentage points of the inventoried ratio.

fig.fig4: **Paper Fig. 4 — CDF (cumulative distribution function) of the incident RF power $P_{\mathrm{in}}$** at the devices, for single-source (reader only) and multi-source (reader + all base stations) harvesting. It decides which devices are in coverage and how fast they harvest.
fig.fig5a: **Paper Fig. 5(a) — single-source harvesting, $L_s = 16$ Msg1 slots per round.** Compares the proposed aperiodic paging with the periodic baseline using $N_g = 1$ or 4 paging groups, with and without mid-round depletion. Only the reader's RF field charges the devices, so many are slow to recharge.
fig.fig5b: **Paper Fig. 5(b) — single-source harvesting, $L_s = 1$.** Same as 5(a) but with one Msg1 slot × $F$ frequencies per round: very short rounds, many collisions.
fig.fig6a: **Paper Fig. 6(a) — multi-source harvesting (reader + 18 base stations), $L_s = 16$.** Aperiodic paging vs. periodic paging with $N_g = 1$ and $N_g = 4$.
fig.fig7: **Paper Fig. 7 — controller comparison** under aperiodic paging (multi-source, $L_1 = 1$): the Recurrent PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) agent adapts $L_s$ and $p_s$ each round; DFSA-Schoute (Dynamic Framed Slotted ALOHA) and CMEBE (Capture-aware Minimum-Error Backlog Estimation) are classic RFID frame-size estimators.
fig.fig8: **Paper Fig. 8 — average resource efficiency** (identified devices per AO, access occasion) vs. number of devices $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$: RL (reinforcement learning) vs. PFSA (Probabilistic Framed Slotted ALOHA) with $L = 1$, 8, 32.
fig.tab4: **Paper Table IV — mid-round depletions per stage**: mean number of devices that run out of energy during paging, Msg1, EI, Msg2 and Msg3 in the Fig. 5 runs.
fig.tab5: **Paper Table V — average identification time (s)** for each controller and $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$.
fig.tab6: **Paper Table VI — effect of the reward weight $\alpha$** on identification time and resource efficiency ($N_{\mathrm{tot}} = 15000$).

curve.aperiodic: **Aperiodic paging (proposed protocol).** The reader pages again right after each round; devices that fail go OFF, recharge and catch a later page. Msg2/Msg3 resources follow the decoded Msg1 via the EI (early indication). No groups ($N_g$ does not apply).
curve.periodic_Ng1: **Periodic paging, $N_g = 1$ (baseline).** All devices form one group and are paged at a fixed interval $T_{\mathrm{periodic}}(L)$; Msg2/Msg3 resources are reserved in advance ($K = 0.5\,L F$).
curve.periodic_Ng4: **Periodic paging, $N_g = 4$ (baseline with 4 paging groups).** Each device joins the group of the first page it catches; the 4 groups are paged in turn, so a device is paged only every 4th round and sleeps synchronously in between.
curve.recurrent_ppo: **Recurrent PPO — Proximal Policy Optimization with a recurrent (LSTM) policy** (paper Sec. IV): chooses $L_s$ and $p_s$ every round from the observed successes, idles and collisions. Needs a trained checkpoint.
curve.dfsa_schoute: **DFSA-Schoute — Dynamic Framed Slotted ALOHA with Schoute's backlog estimate** (backlog ≈ 2.39 × collisions); adapts the frame length $L_s$.
curve.cmebe: **CMEBE — Capture-aware Minimum-Error Backlog Estimation** (Li & Wang); estimates the backlog taking the capture effect into account and adapts the frame length $L_s$.

symbols.title: Symbols used in the paper
symbols.N_tot: **$N_{\mathrm{tot}}$ — total number of deployed devices** (paper: 15000). **$N_{\mathrm{eff}}$** — effective number, i.e. those in coverage.
symbols.N_g: **$N_g$ — number of paging groups** of the periodic baseline. Each device belongs to one group; groups are paged in turn, so with $N_g = 4$ a device is paged every 4th round. The aperiodic protocol has no groups ($N_g = 1$).
symbols.L_s: **$L_s$ — number of Msg1 time slots in round s.** With $F$ frequencies there are $L_s \cdot F$ **AOs (access occasions)**. $L_1$ is the first round's value for adaptive controllers.
symbols.p_s: **$p_s$ — access probability in round s**: a paged device transmits Msg1 with probability $p_s$, otherwise it skips the round.
symbols.F: **$F$ — number of frequency resources** per Msg1 slot (paper: 8).
symbols.alpha: **$\alpha$ (alpha) — reward weight** of the RL (reinforcement learning) agent between identified devices and collisions.
symbols.pfsa: **PFSA/PZE — Probabilistic Framed Slotted ALOHA / Probabilistic Zero Estimator**: $L_s$ fixed, $p_s$ adapted from the number of idle AOs observed in the previous round.
symbols.dep: **w/o depletion — without mid-round depletion**: ablation where devices may go below $E_{\mathrm{low}}$ during a round without turning off.
symbols.E: **$E_{\mathrm{up}}$ / $E_{\mathrm{low}}$ — upper / lower energy threshold**: stored energy at which a device turns on / must turn off.
